absent: Locking, concurrency and memory ordering rules for DRM, AIO, allocation inspection, accounting, ADFS, AFFS and APM objects are not shown.
Entry points, ioctl numbers, system call bindings, error codes and permission checks for the displayed interfaces are not shown.
Validation, negotiation and lifetime behaviour for HDR metadata, atomic commits, format modifiers, blobs, leases, dumb buffers, AIO requests and allocation queries is not shown.
On disk checksum, recovery and geometry interpretation for ADFS and AFFS plus accounting file writing and byte order selection logic are not shown.
APM BIOS call sequence, segment setup and event delivery mechanics beyond state and notification values are not shown.

findings.text: HDR display metadata record starts with single byte transfer function selector and single byte descriptor selector, followed by three primary chromaticity pairs each with two sixteen bit coordinates, then a white point pair of same form, then sixteen bit mastering maximum and minimum plus content maximum and frame average maximum. Chromaticity uses a fine fractional encoding with zero at zero and a fixed large code for unity; luminance maxima use single candela steps and minimum uses a ten thousandth candela step with documented extremes.

HDR output container holds a thirty two bit descriptor selector and a variant area that presently carries one full display metadata record for the HDMI type one case. The variant wrapper preserves container shape while allowing additional descriptor forms later.

Page flip control bits assign event delivery to one, asynchronous flip to two, absolute sequence targeting to four and relative sequence targeting to eight. A target mask joins the two targeting bits and an overall mask joins event plus async plus target bits.

Basic page flip request names a display pipeline and a framebuffer, carries a flag word drawn from the page flip masks, keeps a reserved word, and carries a sixty four bit opaque token that lets callers match completion notification to request.

Targeted page flip request names a display pipeline and a framebuffer, carries a flag word, carries a sequence count for vertical blank targeting, and carries a sixty four bit opaque user token. It differs from the basic form by using the sequence field where the basic form keeps reserved space.

Absolute targeting interprets the sequence field as an exact blank count while relative targeting interprets it as an offset from current count; event and async bits keep their notification and timing roles in both page flip forms.

Dumb buffer creation accepts requested height plus width plus bits per pixel plus flags and returns a handle plus stride plus total size. Mapping accepts a handle with padding and returns a fixed width file offset for a later mapping call that stays compatible across thirty two and sixty four bit callers. Destruction accepts only a handle.

Dumb buffer lifecycle moves from creation to optional mapping and memory mapping and finally to destruction; handle identifies the object across the three steps and pitch plus size outputs from creation describe the mapping.

Atomic commit control reuses event and async bits from page flip and adds test only at hex one hundred, nonblock at hex two hundred and allow modeset at hex four hundred. The combined atomic mask covers those five bits.

Atomic commit descriptor carries a flag word plus object count plus sixty four bit addresses for object identifiers, per object property counts, property identifiers and property values, plus reserved space and a user token for completion correlation.

Format modifier blob header carries version plus flags plus format count with byte offset to format entries plus modifier count with byte offset to modifier entries; data arrays follow the header. Current version is one. Each modifier entry carries a sixty four bit format coverage mask plus a thirty two bit window offset with padding plus a sixty four bit modifier value, so large format lists are covered by sliding sixty four entry windows.
Property blob creation takes a source address plus byte length and returns a new blob identifier; blob destruction takes only that identifier.

Lease creation takes an address of an object identifier array plus object count plus file creation flags and returns a lessee identifier plus a file descriptor. Lessee listing uses a count with padding and a pointer to sixty four bit identifiers; lease content query uses a count with padding and a pointer to thirty two bit object identifiers. Revocation takes only a lessee identifier.

Lessee listing and lease content query share a two call sizing pattern where the caller supplies buffer length on entry and the kernel reports total available on exit while writing at most the supplied length, so a probe call can size a follow up fetch.
Damage rectangle stores four signed thirty two bit edges for opposite corners. Framebuffer close request stores a framebuffer identifier with padding.

Sixty four bit packed pixel places alpha in the top sixteen bit lane, then red, then green, then blue in the lowest lane. Packing limits each component to sixteen bits before shifting; unpacking shifts then limits to sixteen bits. Width adapting forms convert between sixteen bit storage and narrower widths either by rounding division or by shifting away low bits, with per channel helpers for each lane and each conversion style.

Packing and width conversion helpers evaluate channel and width inputs more than once and rely on statement expression temporaries, so inputs with side effects can execute repeatedly. Rounding conversion and shift truncation give different values for the same input, so callers must pick the intended precision rule.
Each examined user header is guarded by a single include once macro that prevents repeated inclusion.
Accounting resource fields use a sixteen bit compact encoding with a thirty two bit companion for wider values; short command length is sixteen characters.

Legacy accounting record holds single byte flag and version, sixteen bit low user and group parts, terminal identifier, thirty two bit creation time, compact user plus system plus elapsed times and memory plus transfer plus block plus fault plus swap counters, an optional sixteen bit tick rate omitted on one architecture under kernel build, thirty two bit exit code, a command field one longer than the short length, split elapsed extension bytes, and full thirty two bit user and group identifiers.

Version three accounting record holds flag plus version plus terminal plus exit code plus user plus group plus process plus parent identifiers plus creation time, an elapsed field whose representation differs between kernel and user views, compact user and system times with resource counters matching legacy roles, and a command field sized exactly to the short length without low identifier parts or tick rate or split extension.

Accounting flag bits mark fork without exec at one, privilege use at two, compatibility mode at four, core dump at eight, signal kill at sixteen and last group member at thirty two. File order marker is hex eighty for big endian and zero for little endian. Format version is two and tick constant aliases kernel tick rate.

Accounting binary layout depends on build context because tick rate padding is conditional and version three elapsed representation changes between kernel and user compilation; command length also differs by one between legacy and version three, so parsers must select layout by version and build.

ADFS disc record is a packed four byte aligned sixty byte on disk layout with single byte geometry and option fields, little endian zone spare plus root plus size plus identifier, a ten character volume name, type plus high size, a nibble split share size with spare bits, a one bit large disc flag with spare bits, high zone count, reserved byte, format version plus root size and trailing spare bytes.
ADFS disc record position is hex C00 with inner offset hex 1C0, total size sixty bytes and bit size eight times byte size.

Rigid disk header stores big endian identity plus checksums plus host plus block size plus flags plus list anchors for bad blocks, partitions, filesystems and drive init, plus geometry, interleave, park, timing, reserved words, cylinder ranges, block counts, auto park interval and fixed length vendor plus product plus revision texts for disk and controller. Partition entry stores big endian identity plus checksums plus host plus next pointer plus flags plus device flags plus a thirty two byte drive name plus reserved and environment arrays.
Rigid disk magic is ASCII RDSK and partition magic is ASCII PART as big endian thirty two bit values; allocation scan limit is sixteen.
Async context handle is an unsigned long value opaque to callers.

Async operation codes assign zero to plain read, one to plain write, two to full sync, three to data sync, five to poll, six to no operation, seven to vector read and eight to vector write; code four is reserved by history for an experimental read.
Async control flag for readiness descriptor is bit zero and control flag for priority inheritance is bit one.
Async completion event reports the submitter cookie plus originating request address as sixty four bit values and primary plus secondary signed sixty four bit result codes.

Async control block carries a user cookie, a kernel assigned key with read write flags whose order depends on byte order, a sixteen bit opcode with priority and file descriptor, buffer address with length and signed offset, a reserved word for future signal delivery, a flag word and an event descriptor consulted when the readiness flag is set. Total size is sixty four bytes.

Control block field order for key versus read write flags swaps between little and big endian builds and unknown byte orders fail compilation, so the wire image is not portable and must be built per target order.

Allocation tag stores module plus function plus file names each limited to sixty four bytes with longer names trimmed, plus a sixty four bit line number. Content identifier wraps a single sixty four bit value.
Allocation counter stores byte total plus call count plus an accuracy byte with padding to eight byte alignment; tag data pairs a full tag with its counter.

Allocation filter selectors enumerate module, function, file, line, accuracy flag and size bounds in order zero through six. Per field masks shift one by selector and the combined mask covers all seven bits. Name limit is sixty four.

Allocation filter carries a sixty four bit selector mask with tag match fields plus minimum and maximum sizes plus an accuracy selector. Positional query carries an input position with a filter and returns tag data on output; accuracy in the filter is a selection criterion while accuracy in the counter reports measurement quality.

Allocation inspection controls use base hex A6 with subcode zero for content identifier, one for positional fetch and two for next entry fetch, exposed as read or read write operations over the matching structures.

Power management event and event detail are sixteen bit unsigned values. BIOS info block reports version plus code segment with offset plus sixteen bit code segment plus data segment plus flags plus lengths for each segment area.

Power states encode ready zero, standby one, suspend two, off three, busy four, reject five and vendor system at hex twenty plus vendor device at hex forty. Enable pair reuses zero for disable and one for enable; engage pair reuses zero for disengage and one for engage.

System power notifications run one through fourteen covering system standby and suspend, normal and critical resume, low battery, status change, time update, critical suspend, user standby and suspend, standby resume, capability change and user hibernation with hibernation resume.

System power lifecycle moves among running, standby, suspend, hibernation and off with user and system request events, resume completion events for each sleep form, and out of band low battery, status, time and capability notices that do not themselves change sleep state.
Display mode header exposes HDR metadata, page flip, dumb buffer, atomic commit, format modifier, blob and lease layouts plus flag and packing helpers for user space display control.
Async interface exposes context handle, control block, completion event, operation codes and control flags for user space submission and reaping.
Allocation inspection exposes tag, counter, filter and positional query layouts with content identifier and fetch controls for user space telemetry.
